pattern: answered controls report the datum frame awaiting acceptance (issue #20)
evidence: Maintainer-approved issue #20 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/20) keeps unanswered defaults as suggestions, so an answered datum-dependent control is omitted until its frame is accepted. The approved review follow-up requires that omission to be visible: Rust adds awaits_datum_frame warnings naming the answered question, required frame and missing datum letters. Python implicitly accepts the frame and reports no pending control. tests/preview.rs, tests/turned_defaults.rs, tests/default_suggestions.rs and the WASM session regression cover position, partial ± locations, runout, flatness and datum controls, clearing the warning and writing semantic PMI after acceptance. Every departure and ordering change is exactly pinned by the documented UPDATE_RULE_DEFAULTS hook in rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz; frozen Python captures are unchanged.

pattern: unanswered defaults remain suggestions until explicitly accepted (issue #20)
evidence: Maintainer-approved decision in specify-core-rust issue #20 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/20): defaults stay suggestions until answered or explicitly accepted; only those are written as PMI, with no provisional drawing. Python preview fills unanswered defaults, but Rust preview/review and IntentEngine.writePmi now use only supplied answers and existing datums. Questions retain suggested values and reasons and unanswered ids remain open; an absent general_tolerance stays absent for draftwright general_tolerance_missing. Position/runout and datum-control answers wait for their datum frames; flatness on A waits for A. They cannot commit an unanswered datum suggestion. CLI/serve apply with explicit accept_defaults is unchanged, and #16 settling does not accept datum or general-tolerance suggestions. tests/default_suggestions.rs and crates/specify-core-wasm/tests/default_suggestions.rs verify GRM-02/GRM-03, partial answers, #16, explicit acceptance and semantic PMI readback; tests/preview.rs guards pending frames. Every complete Python/Rust departure remains pinned in rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz; original captures are unchanged.

pattern: a knurl's teeth derived from DIN 82, which Python's intent does not state
evidence: The maintainer's decision Q4/Q15 (docs/questions.md): AP242's turned_knurl needs at least three of number of teeth, tooth depth, root fillet, helix angle and hand beside the diameters and pitch (WR2; a diamond's helix angle, WR9), so the Rust rules derive them from the knurling standard and state each in the intent with its source, visible and editable ('standard': 'DIN 82', 'derived': key to source). Values: teeth round(pi x 10 / 1) = 31, the pitch kept at the tool's 1 mm; tooth depth P/2 = 0.5, the depth of DIN 82's 90 degree profile (IS 3403:1981 3.1; assumed, no table gives it); root fillet 0.1, the knurling wheel's crest radius up to 1 mm pitch (IS 6776:1980 4.3); a diamond's helix angle 30 degrees and no hand (DIN 82 type RGE). Checked in tests/threads.rs. Python's knurl states pattern, pitch and diameter only.

pattern: axis-first turned datum defaults and their dependent questions and intent
evidence: Axis-first turned datums: plain recognised principal cylinder with greatest total area (diameter breaks ties), excluding thread/knurl answers, recognition and PMI; interrupted shafts may use dominant bosses. Then a perpendicular contact/largest shoulder excluding recess walls unless the sole perpendicular face. Axial holes use diametral position to A alone; other holes keep the full frame. Runout uses A and is not offered on the datum diameter itself. A mostly prismatic body or different principal axes keeps plane datums. tests/turned_defaults.rs checks captured and live corpus geometry, overrides, offsets, cross holes and shoulder contacts. tests/fixtures/rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz is an additional exact regression guard on EVERY changed path and both values (including question ordering and all other rules); rules_oracle asserts that complete list before applying these verdict entries, so these scopes cannot hide further differences. See docs/turned-defaults.md.

pattern: measurement datums are proposed before dimensions, including in ± mode
evidence: Maintainer decision (draftwright-rust #122): choose measurement origins before dimensions. Rust proposes the same geometric A/B/C frame in ± mode and when no feature needs a geometric tolerance; turned parts retain their plain axis A and perpendicular shoulder B. Empty datum answers still remove them. ± hole locations use selected datum planes, never recomputed edge defaults; accepting ± defaults adds no position or geometric-control requirements. General baseline dimensions consequently use the proposed planes too. tests/tolerancing.rs, tests/locations.rs, tests/turned_defaults.rs and tests/writer.rs verify the default path, changed/removed origins, both modes and AP242 DATUM_FEATURE entities with no FCFs. The complete Python and Rust values, including both named no-datum scenarios, are pinned exactly in tests/fixtures/rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz before these verdict entries apply; original Python captures remain unchanged.
